provenance: measured from HPO genes_to_disease + phenotype.hpoa + hp.obo, Reactome UniProt2Reactome_All_Levels + PathwaysRelation, Human Protein Atlas rna_single_cell_type, STRING v12 aliases/info
question: How much of what a disease's causal genes say about its organ systems survives a coarse-graining onto pathways or onto cell types?

estimator.statistic: mutual information I(F;S) in bits, each disease weighted 1
estimator.null: 25 permutations of the disease -> organ-system assignment; every headline is the EXCESS over that null, because MI rises with alphabet size for free
estimator.interval: point +- 1.96 SE, the SE from a 200-resample bootstrap over diseases, each resample carrying its own permuted null. The bootstrap gives the DISPERSION only: mutual information is biased in n, so a percentile interval on a resample holding ~63% of the diseases sits away from the point estimate

morphogenesis_prediction.asks: Does a pathway coarse-graining retain less about systems whose abnormalities are FORMS than about systems whose abnormalities are PROCESSES? Turing 1952 for the mechanism, Ashby 1956 for the representation argument.
morphogenesis_prediction.classification: AUTHORED, and ⚠️ with target contact - the retentions were visible when the classes were written. A description with a p-value, not a pre-registered test. See SYSTEM_CLASS.

systems: Abnormality of prenatal development or birth
Abnormality of blood and blood-forming tissues

morphogenesis_prediction.says: One-sided permutation test on a classification taken from theory rather than fitted, but written with the numbers in view. It cannot show that Turing's mechanism operates in these diseases, and it is not evidence at the strength a pre-registered test would carry. It can show whether the alphabet that describes processes loses more signal in the systems where the theory says form is what fails.
morphogenesis_prediction.p_says: Median over 5 re-derivations of the per-system table, each with its own seed. The single-draw figure this tool used to publish varied from 0.00625 to 0.02185 — more than threefold — because the table it reads is itself estimated against permutation nulls. No seed crossed 0.05, so the direction holds; the magnitude is this range and not a point.

says: Observational mutual information over a static catalogue. NOT effective information and NOT causal emergence: there is no intervention here and no dynamics. It answers whether a coarser alphabet is still informative about the phenotype, not whether it is the causally correct scale.
limits: Organ systems come from HPO annotation, which is curated unevenly - the same ascertainment bias tools/atlas_bias.py measures at +0.2357 on this catalogue.
Genes without a Reactome or HPA mapping drop out of that scale, so the three rows do not stand on identical disease sets; each row reports its own n.
One coarse-graining per scale. A different pathway level or a different enrichment fraction is a different measurement, not a robustness check.
